title: 〜一方(で) / 〜いっぽう(で)
meaning: on one hand… / while… (two contrasting or parallel sides)
simpleExplanation: 〜一方(で) links two facts that stand side by side: "A is true, and at the same time B is true". Often A and B pull in different directions (sociable vs shy), but they can also just be two parallel things one person does (works by day, studies at night).
whenUsed: Common in essays, news and formal speech when describing two sides of a situation, a person or a trend. It can also start a new sentence: 一方、〜 ("meanwhile / on the other hand"). Less common in casual chat, where people say 〜けど or 〜が.
formation: な-adjective + な / である + 一方(で)
Noun + である + 一方(で)

diagram.translation: While my older brother is sociable, my younger brother is shy.

examples.ja: 兄は社交的な一方で、弟は内気だ。
examples.reading: あにはしゃこうてきないっぽうで、おとうとはうちきだ。
examples.en: While my older brother is sociable, my younger brother is shy.
examples.note: な-adjective + な + 一方で. Two different subjects are contrasted.

examples.ja: 彼は会社で働く一方、夜は大学で勉強している。
examples.reading: かれはかいしゃではたらくいっぽう、よるはだいがくでべんきょうしている。
examples.en: He works at a company, while at night he studies at university.
examples.note: Same subject, two parallel activities. で can be dropped.

examples.ja: 都市の人口が増える一方で、地方は減っている。
examples.reading: としのじんこうがふえるいっぽうで、ちほうはへっている。
examples.en: While urban populations grow, rural ones are shrinking.
examples.note: A trend and its opposite side by side.

examples.ja: この薬はよく効く一方で、副作用も強い。
examples.reading: このくすりはよくきくいっぽうで、ふくさようもつよい。
examples.en: This medicine works well, but on the other hand its side effects are strong.
examples.note: Plus and minus of the same thing.

examples.ja: 輸出は好調だ。一方、国内の売り上げは伸びていない。
examples.reading: ゆしゅつはこうちょうだ。いっぽう、こくないのうりあげはのびていない。
examples.en: Exports are strong. Meanwhile, domestic sales are not growing.
examples.note: Sentence-initial 一方、 introduces the other side.

similarGrammar.difference: Also 'on the other hand', but the two sides must belong to the same thing and be clearly plus/minus. 一方で is broader and can contrast different subjects.
Completely different meaning: 'keeps on …ing' (one-directional change). Attaches only to verbs of change.
'In contrast to' — sharper contrast between two subjects, often with numbers or facts.

commonMistakes.wrong: 都市の人口は増える一方で。
commonMistakes.right: 都市の人口は増える一方だ。
commonMistakes.why: If you mean 'keeps on increasing' you need 一方だ. 一方で must be followed by a second clause.

commonMistakes.wrong: 彼は社交的一方で、弟は内気だ。
commonMistakes.right: 彼は社交的な一方で、弟は内気だ。
commonMistakes.why: な-adjectives need な (or である) before 一方.

commonMistakes.wrong: 私は学生の一方で、働いている。
commonMistakes.right: 私は学生である一方で、働いている。
commonMistakes.why: Nouns take である, not の, before 一方で.

usageNotes: 一方で often appears in analytical writing: 〜が増える一方で、〜は減っている.
The two clauses do not have to be opposites; they can simply be two things happening in parallel.
Sentence-initial 一方、 is followed by a comma and starts a fresh contrast, much like 'Meanwhile'.
jlptTips: If the blank is followed by a full second clause with a different subject or a contrasting fact, 一方で fits; if the sentence ends right after the blank, it is 一方だ.
反面 vs 一方で: check whether both halves describe the same thing (反面) or different things (一方で).
In 並べ替え, 一方で normally comes right after な / である / a plain verb, never after a noun alone.
